# Hannune

> A Seoul-based AI engineer who automates the document work companies
still do by hand: translation, data extraction, summarizing and review,
and converting one document into the form the next one needs. Two things
set the work apart. First, formatting survives: multi-column layouts,
nested tables, numbering, and styles come back the way they went in,
which is where general translation tools break down. Second, extracted
figures are reconciled: line items are checked against the summary
totals elsewhere in the document, so a number that does not add up is
flagged rather than shipped. That second part runs as a public demo at
https://demo.hannune.ai/validation/, where an uploaded spreadsheet or
text-layer PDF comes back with the cell location, expected value and
actual value of every mismatch. Founded 2021. 8+ years of production AI
experience across Netflix, Sony, and LG Energy Solution. 2 AI
optimization patents registered in South Korea.

## What we do

1. **Document Automation** (primary service). Fixed-scope engagements to
   automate document translation, extraction, review, and format
   conversion. Deployment is a customer choice, not a constraint: the
   pipeline runs in the customer's cloud account, on their own servers,
   or air-gapped. Three packages: Starter ($8,999, 3 weeks, one document
   type run end to end on the customer's real files), Standard ($38,999,
   6 weeks, several document types in production with batch processing
   and consistency checks), Enterprise (custom pricing, 12+ weeks,
   document workflows across teams inside the customer's own
   infrastructure). Plus Ops Retainer (from $3,499/month) for ongoing
   accuracy passes, new templates, and terminology updates. Retrieval and
   agent technology (Graph RAG over Neo4j, LangGraph multi-agent
   pipelines, cross-lingual entity resolution) is used underneath where
   it earns its place, but the deliverable is the document workflow.

2. **Entity Resolution API** (product) — A SaaS subscription product,
   available now. Public tier pricing ($0/$19/$99/$499 per month), free
   tier included. Built on Splink with LLM disambiguation. Hosted at
   app.hannune.ai, pricing and sign-up at app.hannune.ai/entity-resolution.

3. **Ownership API** — A SaaS subscription product (beta 2026)
   unifying Northeast Asia 5%-rule and acquisition filings (Korea
   OpenDART, Japan EDINET, China CNINFO, Hong Kong HKEX, Taiwan
   TWSE, US SEC EDGAR ADRs) into one cross-lingual ownership graph.
   Cross-lingual Entity Resolution (Korean/Japanese/Chinese/English)
   to a single canonical ID. Public tier pricing ($0 Free, $49
   Developer, $199 Professional, $999 Business, Enterprise custom),
   roughly one tenth of comparable enterprise alternatives like
   Sayari Graph or Moody's Orbis. Documented at
   https://hannune.ai/ownership.html. Shares one API key with
   Entity Resolution API at app.hannune.ai.

4. **2asy.ai** (platform). A Northeast Asia (Korea, Japan, China, Hong
   Kong) risk and compliance intelligence platform: the same document
   pipeline pointed at public filings instead of client files. A separate
   product hosted at 2asy.ai.

## Recent work

- Format-preserving translation pipeline (Hannune's own system, not a
  client delivery): a docx-to-docx pipeline built in-house. Layout,
  tables, numbering, and styles are preserved, approved terminology is
  enforced from a glossary, do-not-translate terms are locked before
  the model sees them, and a translation memory reuses prior approved
  sentences. Further languages can be added without rebuilding it.
- Medical device manufacturer (IVD): eight completed sessions of
  in-house AI engineering training for the client's internal committee.
- Gahyun Tax Accounting (2024): Korean-language search over tax code,
  precedents, and case files. Search time for one answer fell from
  up to 5 hours to under 40 minutes, with accuracy improved by over
  50%. Knowledge-graph retrieval underneath.
- LG Energy Solution: LangGraph-based multi-agent pipeline for
  global talent data acquisition, integrating Crawl4AI and EXAONE.
- Scenera (TnM AI): Enterprise AI systems for multiple sectors.

## Technical stack

Python, FastAPI, Docker, LangChain, LangGraph, Neo4j, ElasticSearch,
Crawl4AI, EXAONE, LiteLLM. Format-preserving document processing
(docx, multi-column PDF), Korean-language NLP, and cross-lingual
(Korean / Japanese / Chinese / English) document work as the core
specialties.

## Writing

Build-in-public essays on Claude Code, Graph RAG, entity resolution,
and operating autonomous AI agents. Index at https://hannune.ai/blog/

- Why I built AI Agent Framework Compare: a directory, not a benchmark
  (2026-07-02): Four production agent projects in two years, four
  different frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, OpenAI Agents
  SDK), and two weeks of doc-reading plus toy demos every single time.
  Public agent benchmarks measure canned tool-call success and miss
  the three things that actually decide a real project: state-model
  fit, abstraction escape, and failure recovery. So the reference
  I kept wishing existed was a directory of framework rows, not a
  benchmark. Fifteen frameworks at launch, one row each, with
  control style, state model, license, one-line shape-of tagline,
  and GitHub stars as a rough liveness signal. Data file is open
  for one-line PR corrections. Live at compare-lab.xyz.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/why-i-built-ai-agent-framework-compare.html

- When the same incident becomes five separate events in your graph
  (2026-06-30): A single East Asian merger is filed at OpenDART in
  Korean, EDINET in Japanese, and a Hong Kong exchange in Chinese,
  plus an English wire story. A one-document-per-LLM graph builder
  extracts each in isolation, so one incident becomes four Event
  nodes. Cross-document event coreference is a different problem
  from entity resolution: even with entities unified, the events
  stay split. Deduping by summary text fails because cross-language
  token overlap is near zero and same-language overlap is noisy.
  The fix is a two-stage resolver: a rule filter (shared entity,
  72-hour window, Jaccard or event-type match) to bound LLM cost,
  a three-way same / related / distinct judgment, and union-find
  clustering on the "same" verdicts. Read-only against Neo4j.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/cross-document-event-coreference.html

- Claude Code hallucinations: three cases, one fix (2026-06-24):
  Three real Claude Code hallucinations caught in two weeks while
  running it daily for development and research: dead code stated
  as live, a sub-agent fabricating measurements that looked like
  real data, and stale context held as fact. The fix is not a
  better prompt. It is an external premise-resistance gate that
  runs before the main agent answers anything claim-shaped, plus
  a session-start context diet, memory frontmatter with active /
  superseded status, and a deterministic prompt hook that triggers
  the gate. Self-verification is unreliable. External gates work.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/claude-code-hallucination-discipline.html

- How I Turned Claude Code Into the Operator of a One-Person AI Company
  (2026-05-26): Moving Claude Code from autocomplete to a production
  operator using a layered CLAUDE.md, seven sub-agents, persistent
  memory, and hard guardrails enforced by hooks. Core thesis: the hard
  part of production AI agents is operational discipline, not prompting.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/claude-code-production-operator.html

- The Real Work in Graph RAG Is Not Extraction (2026-05-26): Building
  the seed knowledge graph for 2asy.ai. Extraction is the easy part.
  The real work is normalization: collapsing 360 relation types into
  80 canonical forms, merging duplicate entities, and fixing evidence
  so the causal graph is walkable. Runs on local GPU hardware.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/graph-rag-normalization.html

- Entity Resolution as an API: How I Built It, Over-Fit It, and Fixed
  It (2026-05-26): Turning entity resolution into a single API call by
  wrapping Splink (open-source, UK Ministry of Justice) with a registry
  that learns aliases over time. Includes an honest account of over-
  fitting a self-built evaluation set and fixing it with a held-out set.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/entity-resolution-api.html

- How I Caught My LLM Fabricating Its Own Evidence (2026-05-30): In the
  2asy.ai knowledge graph the model fabricated the evidence quotes behind
  its own relations, stitching distant sentences together with ellipses.
  Truncating article input made it worse. The fix is a deterministic
  substring check at commit time (the evidence must appear verbatim in the
  source) plus full-body-or-skip collection. Over 500 documents cleaned.
  Core thesis: verify a generator's output with code, not another generator.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/graph-rag-fabricated-evidence.html

- From Vector Search to a Cross-Domain Ontology Graph: How 2asy.ai Reads
  Tariff News (2026-06-03): The retrieval behind 2asy.ai evolved in three
  steps. Plain vector RAG could find similar passages but not represent
  causality. A simple per-article Graph RAG could follow a chain inside one
  document but produced isolated per-document graphs that could not connect
  a cause in one article to its effect in another. The current version runs
  a cross-domain ontology Graph RAG: a shared set of entity, event, and
  relation types plus entity resolution across documents, so the same
  real-world entity becomes one node and causal edges span domains. The
  latest tariff briefing renders its actual causal graph on the page (around
  41 nodes and 60 edges, focused on a Sunset Review root and bridge nodes).
  The graph is thin and partly untyped today; this is a data-accumulation
  problem, not a design ceiling, and it gets denser as more documents flow
  through the same ontology. Runs on local GPU hardware (RTX 4090, W6800).
  https://hannune.ai/blog/cross-domain-ontology-graph-rag.html

- Cross-Lingual Entity Resolution in a Trade Knowledge Graph: Adding 39,534
  Aliases to 6,883 Nodes (2026-06-07): 2asy.ai reads English trade news, but
  entities appear in their local-language forms (for example the Korean,
  Japanese, and Chinese names for Bank of Korea or Samsung Electronics).
  Without cross-lingual resolution each foreign-language mention becomes a
  separate node and causal chains break at the language boundary. The fix was
  to fill the registry alias tables, not rewrite the resolver: 39,534 ko/ja/zh
  aliases added across 6,883 of the 13,371 canonical entities. A collision
  check and a confidence gate excluded only 8 candidates (3 CENTCOM collisions
  already mapped elsewhere, 5 held because no verified local-language name was
  found). The aliases are validated on the local ER registry; rollout to the
  live 2asy.ai graph is pending. Lesson: in Graph RAG, resolution caps
  extraction quality, and cross-lingual resolution is a prerequisite for a
  coherent multilingual graph.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/cross-lingual-entity-resolution.html

- I Built a Local LLM Rig to Escape API Bills. Then I Paid OpenAI Again.
  (2026-06-13): 2asy.ai needs thousands of single-document extractions per
  cycle for the Graph RAG pipeline, all under one strict rule: no cross-
  document attention (no concatenated prompts, no shared context). Four
  options were tested against that rule. Local Gemma 4 27B on a Ryzen-class
  4090 plus W6800 ran fine on llama.cpp but was blocked from vLLM by an
  unsupported 4-bit MoE path and a CUDA 12.9 versus 12.8 driver gap; live
  serving and multimodal lanes still belong here. OpenRouter has no real
  batch endpoint, only live pricing with 2 to 17 second latency, occasional
  121 second timeouts and 429 caps. Gemini batch through the official Python
  SDK silently inline-concatenated the documents into one prompt, which
  leaked context across rows and forced a Neo4j rollback (upstream issue
  googleapis/python-genai 1984, not-planned). OpenAI Batch on gpt-5.4-mini
  passed the test: JSONL line-isolated requests, 50% discount, around 2.7
  minutes for a 100-document nano gate, zero 429s, around one cent per
  document. The decision is per-pipeline, not per-company: the batch lane
  moved to OpenAI, the local rig kept the live serving and multimodal lanes.
  Local LLM advocacy belongs to lanes, not to companies.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/local-llm-to-openai-batch.html
